To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ketoprofen plus UV-A radiation induces the production of TNF-α and IL-6 in murine Langerhans cell cultures, that these cytokines are important in the induction of photocontact dermatitis, that IL-6 and IL-8 are involved in the migration of Langerhansen cells to draining lymph nodes and that the migration of LCA-3+ cells to the draining lymph nodes is increased after ketoprofen plus irradiation.
ketoprofen plus UV-A irradiation induces the release of IL-6 and IL-10 from murine LCs and that these effects are mediated through the activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR).
ketoprofen is a potent photocontact allergen, and that it is not a phototoxic agent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel and efficient methods for the synthesis of 2-substituted 3,4-diarylfurans and their application in the synthesis of biologically active molecules.
the study of the effects of ketoprofen plus UV-A radiation (K+UV-A) in murine photoallergic contact dermatitis.
the development of novel, efficient and environmentally friendly processes for the preparation of ketoprofen and its derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of an association between the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and the risk of developing skin cancer.
there are no data available that can be considered as conclusive for the carcinogenic potential of ketoprofen.
the results of our study do not support the hypothesis of a photocontact reaction between ketoprofen and UV radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the study indicate a significant increase in the expression of the genes of interest in the presence of ketoprofen.
the results of this study indicate that a combination of UVA and ketoprofen may be a potential treatment for photocontact dermatitis.
the ketoprofen plus UV-A combination is able to induce a significant increase in the number of Langerhansen cells, which is not the case for the ketoprofen alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ketoprofen is a very potent inhibitor of the enzyme COX-2 and is a good candidate for further study as a possible treatment for cancer.
the use of ketoprofen in patients with chronic pain is not associated with a greater risk for cardiovascular adverse effects.
ketoprofen is not a safe ingredient for use in sunscreens and should not be used.
